questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Djibouti?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Djibouti on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Djibouti article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Eritrea in the north, Ethiopia in the west and south, and Awdal of Somalia in the southeast.

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of Djibouti is Djibouti.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Djibouti article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of Djibouti is Djibouti.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Djibouti?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Djibouti is the Djiboutian franc.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Djibouti on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Djibouti on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Djibouti?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Djiboutians” part of the Djibouti article.

questions.proof: It has many languages - though Somali and Afar are the most widely spoken ones, Arabic and French serve as the official languages.
